description: AI WaterWise Kerala is a solo project team focused on artificial intelligence, environmental monitoring, smart agriculture and water management. Our project uses NASA POWER data to analyse rainfall and temperature patterns across Kerala's 14 districts. We aim to explore innovative technology solutions for climate awareness, drought-risk monitoring and sustainable farming.
summary: AI WaterWise Kerala is an AI-powered agricultural and environmental monitoring web application that uses NASA POWER rainfall and temperature data to analyse climate patterns across all 14 districts of Kerala. It identifies unusual climate conditions, assesses potential drought risks and provides farmer-oriented recommendations. Through an interactive Streamlit dashboard, users can explore district-level rainfall, temperature, climate anomalies and risk categories. The project aims to transform NASA's open climate data into accessible information that supports climate awareness, agricultural planning and sustainable water management.
details:
Problem Statement Agriculture and water management are affected by changes in rainfall and temperature. Understanding climate variations is important for farmers to make informed agricultural and water-management decisions. Proposed Solution AI WaterWise Kerala is a district-level environmental monitoring and agricultural decision-support web application developed using NASA POWER climate data. Objectives - Monitor rainfall and temperature across 14 districts of Kerala. - Analyse monthly rainfall and yearly average temperature. - Identify unusual climate conditions. - Assess potential drought risks. - Generate farmer-oriented recommendations. Methodology 1. Collect historical rainfall and temperature data from NASA POWER. 2. Process and organise data for all 14 Kerala districts. 3. Calculate monthly rainfall and yearly temperature summaries. 4. Calculate rainfall and temperature anomalies. 5. Classify climate conditions into Normal Condition and Unusual Condition. 6. Categorise drought risks into Normal, Watch and Severe Dry Conditions. 7. Generate recommendations and display the results through a Streamlit dashboard. Technologies Used - Python - Pandas and NumPy - Scikit-learn - Matplotlib - Streamlit - Google Colab - GitHub - NASA POWER Project Results The processed dataset contains 7,714 monthly records covering 14 Kerala districts. The condition classification produced 7,096 Normal Condition labels and 618 Unusual Condition labels. Expected Impact The application makes historical climate information easier to understand and supports agricultural awareness, climate monitoring and sustainable water-management decisions. Limitations and Future Scope The current prototype uses historical climate data and defined drought-risk thresholds. It is not an official weather forecasting or warning system. Future improvements include real-time weather updates, crop-specific recommendations and early-warning notifications. AI Assistance Acknowledgement ChatGPT was used for coding guidance, explanations, documentation and presentation preparation. AI and machine-learning techniques were incorporated into the climate-condition analysis.
